name: John J. O'Connor
description: MNHS associates O’Connor with the protection arrangement beginning in 1900 and records his retirement in 1920.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: William 'Reddy' Griffin
description: MNHS describes Griffin as an early intermediary, preceding Hogan in the role.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: Dan 'Dapper Dan' Hogan
role: Proprietor of the Green Lantern Saloon and underworld broker
description: MNHS associates Hogan with the Green Lantern and records his death in a 1928 car bombing.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: Leon Gleckman
aliases: The Al Capone of Saint Paul
role: Bootlegging syndicate leader and political powerbroker
description: The hotel’s retrospective associates Gleckman with a suite there. The appellate opinions separately document his tax and contempt cases.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: Bernard Fuchs
role: Juror in the 1934 Gleckman federal tax trial
description: The 1938 opinion in Gleckman’s contempt case describes payments and credit involving juror Fuchs. It does not support portraying him as the sole juror preventing conviction.
qualifications: This project does not establish a separate conviction of Fuchs.

name: William Hamm Jr.
role: President of the Theo. Hamm Brewing Company; victim
description: Hamm was kidnapped in June 1933, held for ransom, and released alive. The examined sources differ about the precise abduction setting.
qualifications: The RCHS account identifies a former residence; the FBI retrospective describes Hamm leaving his office. The precise abduction footprint is unresolved in this project.

name: Edward G. Bremer
role: President of Commercial State Bank; victim
description: The federal summary dates Bremer’s abduction to January 17, 1934. The FBI retrospective reports his release after roughly three weeks.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: Walter W. Magee
role: Saint Paul contractor and Bremer family friend; intermediary
description: The investigative summary describes Magee receiving coercive communications and notifying authorities.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: Harry Sawyer
role: Underworld finger man and Barker-Karpis associate
description: Investigators attributed to Sawyer a preference for kidnapping Bremer over robbing his bank.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: John Dillinger
description: The FBI retrospective describes Dillinger’s use of an alias, the Lincoln Court confrontation, and his wounded escape.
qualifications: Castle Royal attendance remains disputed. The Lincoln Court sequence here is attributed to the FBI retrospective.

name: Evelyn 'Billie' Frechette
description: The FBI retrospective places Frechette at Lincoln Court and reports her later conviction for conspiracy to harbor a fugitive.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.

name: Homer Van Meter
description: The FBI retrospective describes Van Meter’s involvement in the Lincoln Court confrontation.
qualifications: Read the linked claims for attribution and limits; association does not establish uncharged conduct.
